result.summary:
Rework iteration 1 of docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md, addressing the single MAJOR finding in handoffs/WF02-REQ-031/step-01b-code-design-validator.json (commit 6c127e2, evaluated commit cd4b9f3): the force_reply ref-line disambiguation mechanism (Sec1.2/Sec3.1/Sec6.3) encoded only the registration id, not which of the three sibling optional fields (liked/improve/topicVotes) a given prompt was for, so a reply to an OLD, already-answered prompt for one field (e.g. liked) arriving after the flow advanced to a different field (e.g. improve) was silently written to the CURRENTLY-expected field instead of being recognized as stale -- contradicting Sec6.3 step 8's own claim that stale replies are 'silently ignored.' Applied option (a) from the validator's two offered fixes (encode the field, recheck it at write time), not option (b) (documenting misattribution as an accepted tradeoff) -- per the task's own instruction, silent misattribution is not an acceptable tradeoff for a feedback flow. docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md was NOT touched, per the validator's own statement that no schema change is needed for this fix (the field name lives in the force_reply message text, not a new stored column) -- confirmed true: no new column was added anywhere in this rework.

Concrete changes to docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md:

1. Sec1.2 (resolution paragraph): rewritten so the disambiguation mechanism is now stated as encoding BOTH a 'Feedback ref: <registrationId>' line AND a new 'Feedback field: <fieldName>' line in every liked/improve/topicVotes force_reply prompt's own text. The generic text listener now extracts both the registration id AND the field the REPLIED-TO message was actually for, and proceeds only when the freshly-derived currently-expected field (Sec2.2/Sec2.7) matches the field encoded in the message actually replied to -- a mismatch is now explicitly a no-op, named as the same 'recheck at write time' pattern this design's own checkin/QR-style stale-tap gates already use elsewhere (Sec6.1 step 9, Sec6.2 step 9), making REQ-031 internally consistent with its own established convention instead of asserting an unimplemented guarantee.

2. Sec3.1: formatFeedbackTextPrompt gained a third parameter, field: FeedbackOptionalField, and its rule now specifies rendering the second 'Feedback field: ' line. ParseFeedbackReplyResult's ok:true variant gained a field: FeedbackOptionalField member; parseFeedbackReplyContext's rule now specifies extracting and validating that second line (must equal exactly one of the three FeedbackOptionalField literals) in addition to the existing registrationId extraction, returning ok:false if either line is missing or the field value is not one of the three exact literals.

3. Sec6.3 (the generic reply-to-message text listener): step 8 rewritten -- the existing two clauses (step.kind !== "feedback-field", step.field === "nps") are unchanged, and a third clause is added: step.field !== parsed.field. This third clause is the actual fix -- it is what makes the previously-false 'stale reply ... silently ignored' claim true for the specific case the validator traced (a reply to a superseded prompt for a different-but-still-valid sibling field). Steps 10-11 unchanged in logic (still use step.field to write), with a note added clarifying step.field and parsed.field are guaranteed equal after step 8's gate passes.

4. Sec6.4 (advanceFeedbackFlow) step 3: clarified that formatFeedbackTextPrompt is called with step.field as its field argument, so every freshly-sent prompt's own ref line always correctly names the field it is actually for.

5. Sec7 (i18n catalog): added a new fieldLinePrefix key (the literal "Feedback field: ", fixed/non-localized exactly like the existing refLinePrefix, for the identical reason -- both are machine-parseable anchors enforced present-in-both-locales by catalogs.test.ts's existing runtime parity check, REQ-013 Sec4) and updated the surrounding note to cover both prefixes together.

6. Sec8 (AC map): AC3's row extended to cite Sec3.1's two-line ref/field encoding plus Sec6.3 step 8's field-match gate as what makes each answer/skip land on the correct one of the three sibling optional fields rather than a misattributed one.

Nothing else in the design was touched -- Sec0/Sec2.1-2.6/Sec4/Sec5/Sec6.1/Sec6.2/Sec6.5/Sec9/Sec10 are unchanged verbatim from the version the validator already checked and passed on every other point. docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md is unchanged (confirmed: no new column, no DDL change needed for this fix).
